questions.question: What does it mean to listen for "gist"?
options: To understand the main idea without catching every word
To write down every word you hear
To focus only on numbers and names
To translate each sentence into Norwegian
questions.explanation: Listening for gist means trying to understand what something is about in broad terms. It is the listening version of skimming in reading.

questions.question: What is the difference between active and passive listening?
options: Active listening means concentrating fully and trying to understand; passive listening is just hearing sounds
Active listening means talking while you listen; passive listening means staying quiet
Active listening is for music; passive listening is for speech
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Active listening means you concentrate, ask questions in your head and connect what you hear to what you already know. Passive listening is hearing sounds without really trying to understand.

questions.question: Which words in a sentence are usually the "key words"?
options: Nouns, verbs and adjectives
Articles and prepositions
Only the first and last word
Pronouns like "it" and "they"
questions.explanation: Key words carry the most meaning in a sentence, and they are usually nouns, verbs and adjectives.

questions.question: You listen to a podcast to find out exactly what time an event starts. What kind of listening is this?
options: Listening for specific information
Listening for gist
Listening for attitude
Predicting
questions.explanation: When you listen for details like times, names or numbers, you are listening for specific information, not just the general idea.

questions.question: Which of these is good advice for improving your listening comprehension?
options: Listen to English every day and don't panic when you miss some words
Only listen to one speaker so you never hear different accents
Always translate every word into Norwegian while listening
Avoid subtitles completely from the start
questions.explanation: Daily listening, focusing on what you do understand, and gradually moving from Norwegian to English subtitles are recommended strategies. Hearing different accents is also useful.
